name: Nexkin ArcGuard Insulated Shock Handler
description:
Rubberized dielectric outer shell over a compressed aerogel mid-layer and a moisture-wicking interior mesh. Rated to 40kV dry contact — the standard for live-line electrical maintenance in M88's aging infrastructure grid. The knuckle and palm zones are double-layered; fingertips are single-layer for better feel on terminal contacts. Color is safety yellow with black palm panels, mandated by Tier 2 transit and utility standards.

A wide gauntlet cuff seals over standard work sleeves with a velcro-and-snap system. Versions with an extended chrome-flange channel are available through Nexkin's augment-worker program at a modest surcharge.
functionality: Rated 40kV dry contact insulation; aerogel mid-layer provides thermal buffer against arc flash; double-palm reinforcement for grip durability; gauntlet cuff seals over work sleeves; chrome-flange channel variant available for augmented workers.
what_it_says: You touch the grid with your hands and you've made your peace with that.
story_hooks: A worker survives a 60kV surge that should have killed them — the gloves were rated 40kV, and someone needs to know why they held.
A pair is found in a transit tunnel where there's no scheduled maintenance work, with scorch marks on the palm that don't match any known grid fault location.
The chrome-flange channel variant is being quietly sold on the Shelf without the standard rating certification — someone is cutting costs on the dielectric layer.
